frostTender.notes: Corroborated directly for gem squash: Starke Ayres' Gem Squash Production Guideline states 'They are frost-sensitive and grow best under warm conditions.'

evidence.quote: Most gem squash is direct-sown, that is the seed is planted directly into the soil.

summer.notes: No gem-squash-specific sowing-calendar row exists; the generic 'Cucurbits' row is used as the regional proxy, the same approach already applied to the 'pumpkin' catalog entry.

evidence.doc: KZN DARD, 'Plant Establishment' (Vegetable Production series), Table 6, generic 'Cucurbits' row, 'Hot areas' column

evidence.doc: KZN DARD, 'Plant Establishment' (Vegetable Production series), Table 6, generic 'Cucurbits' row, 'Warm areas' column

evidence.quote: Approximately 50 - 60 days to maturity for Baby Gems, and 70 - 80 days for mature fruit.
evidence.doc: Starke Ayres, product page for 'Pinnacle' gem squash hybrid

daysToHarvestRange.notes: Range spans picking as immature 'baby gem' (50-60 days) through to mature fruit (70-80 days). A real-farm case study (Starke Ayres news article, Brits, North West) reported first picking '81 days after sowing', slightly above the upper bound, likely reflecting field rather than trial conditions.

yield.conditions: Conservative 12 t/ha, likely 15-18 t/ha, target 25-30 t/ha (KZN); a commercial case study near Brits, North West targeted 'around 30 ton per hectare'

evidence.doc: KZN DARD, 'Expected Yields' (Vegetable Production series), Table 8

varieties.name: Pinnacle
varieties.notes: Compact/restricted-habit hybrid with ZYMV and powdery-mildew tolerance; used commercially near Brits, North West in a Starke Ayres case study (direct-seeded from 1 August, ~12,000-13,000 plants/ha, ~30 t/ha target). Company markets it nationally; the lowveld-bushveld tag reflects the case-study region, not an exclusive recommendation.

varieties.name: STAR 8001
varieties.notes: Listed by Starke Ayres as a baby-gem hybrid product; only the name/title was retrievable from a JS-rendered catalogue listing this session, so no maturity or zone claim is made.

zoneNotes: A Starke Ayres case study near Brits (North West, lowveld-bushveld-type climate) describes the area as having 'short, mild winters with some frost-free areas', allowing direct seeding 'as early as [1] August' with four staggered plantings totalling 52ha between August and October, broadly consistent with the KZN DARD 'Warm areas' Cucurbits window used for the mild-frost pattern above.
gaps: Winter/Western Cape sowMonths not sourced: KZN DARD's sowing calendar is KZN-specific (Cold/Warm/Hot-area columns) and has no Western Cape column, and no Western Cape/Elsenburg-specific cucurbit sowing calendar was found this session. Gem squash is certainly grown in the Western Cape (Starke Ayres' Pinnacle product page references a 'winter production' population figure of 15,000-18,000 plants/ha), so this is recorded as a genuine gap, not an empty array implying the crop isn't grown there.
Harvest period duration (how many weeks/months a planting keeps producing, as distinct from days-to-first-harvest) is not sourced specifically for gem squash.

Row/in-row spacing is sourced via KZN DARD's generic 'Squash, trailing' table row rather than a gem-squash-specific spacing trial, following the same regional-proxy approach already used for the catalog's 'pumpkin' entry.
STAR 8001 variety details (maturity, recommended zones) could not be verified beyond its product name.
summary: Frost tenderness, transplant status, days-to-harvest, row/in-row spacing, seed rate and yield are all sourced (KZN DARD Tables 5/8 plus Starke Ayres' Gem Squash Guideline and Pinnacle product page). Verdict held to 'partial' because winter/Western Cape sowMonths could not be sourced this session.
